experiments.conditions: Faired open-water characteristics of the series at Rn(0.75R) = 2e6 (Oosterveld & van Oossanen 1975 Table 5 polynomials, regression of the NSMB tests corrected to Rn = 2e6 by Lerbs' equivalent-profile method). Each row carries rpm so that Rn(0.75R) = 2e6 for the assumed D = 0.24 m (and v_ms = J n D).
experiments.source: Oosterveld & van Oossanen (1975), ISP 22(251), Table 5 (polynomial coefficients copied, evaluated for Z = 4, AE/A0 = 0.70, P/D = 1.0)
experiments.uncertainty: not raw data: regression of model tests; deviation from the original test points of order +-2-3 % in KT/KQ (paper); implementation cross-checked (B5-75 P/D 1.0 J 0.64: KT 0.220 vs 0.223 in MIT 2.611 notes)

sources.citation: Oosterveld M.W.C., van Oossanen P. (1975). Further computer-analyzed data of the Wageningen B-screw series. International Shipbuilding Progress 22(251), 251-262. Tables 1-5, eq. 7.

Kuiper G. (1992). The Wageningen Propeller Series. MARIN Publication 92-001, Wageningen. Ch. 4 (geometry of the B-series: Fig. 4.1 pitch distribution of the four-bladed series, sect. 4.5 pitch on the face, 4.7 rake 15 deg, 4.8 hub 1/6 D, Tables 4.1-4.12).
Foeth E.J. (2019). Remodeling the B-series geometry in a CAD environment. Sixth Int. Symp. on Marine Propulsors smp'19, Rome (sections defined from the pressure side; context).

notes: A family benchmark: the geometry is generated exactly from the series definition (contour K(r), t/D = Ar - Br Z, max-thickness position, V1/V2 section functions) and the performance is the series' own Rn = 2e6 polynomial - so the case tests BEM against 'what the B-series charts say'. Other P/D (0.5-1.4), AE/A0 or Z can be produced by editing PD/EAR/Z in extraction/build_b4_70.py (twist changes non-uniformly with P/D, so a P/D change is NOT a global pitch offset). ASSUMPTIONS: D = 0.24 m (dimensionless case); section edge thickness 0 with a rounded nose over the first 5 % of the LE-to-max-thickness distance (the series tables end in a wedge; Kuiper mentions ~0.2 tmax edge thickness on the models); four-bladed pitch reduction at 0.2-0.5R included (as tested; Kuiper: effect negligible); 15 deg rake and the small skew ignored; tip contour 0.9-1.0R shaped like the BB-series. Twist = face-pitch angle + nose-tail-line angle of the generated section (<= 0.53 deg, inside 0.6R only). Hub d/D = 1/6 (Rhub = 0.02 m), blade data from 0.2R. The polynomials assume turbulent-friction scaling to Rn = 2e6; XFOIL free-transition polars (Ncrit 9) give lower section drag, so BEM KQ is expected slightly low.
